quotes.text: So, AI is one of the most important developments because of what it is able to provide as an analytical capability and assistance.

And I don’t think AI should ever be used with respect to any decision making with respect to nuclear weapons, or even as we look to the prosecution of conflicts. Obviously, strategy, the assessment, discernment, it’s going to be incredibly important. But decision making should remain with the human factor.

Our biggest threat in AI is that our adversaries get there first. [...] The utilization of AI for an authoritarian regime is probably the biggest threat that we have seen in the longest time to mankind and to the issue of freedom and liberty.

As artificial intelligence and quantum computing continue to reshape the world, it is crucial for lawmakers to have a better understanding of their implications and potential. [...] With countries like Russia and China investing in these technologies, the United States needs to harness the full potential of both AI and quantum computing to drive economic growth, enhance national security, and improve the daily lives of Americans.

One of the primary reasons the United States military remains the most capable and lethal fighting force in the world is our technological advantage. I am proud to support projects like the Laboratory Revitalization Program which increased the ceiling for defense laboratory minor construction from $9 million to $12 million to support research facilities like the Air Force Research Lab.

The Flyer supercomputer represents a significant investment at @WrightPattAFB that brings new levels of capabilities in modeling, artificial intelligence, computing, and more with new technology.
